content: 1. The study conducted across 195 countries and territories from 1990 to 2016 was published in The Lancet in 2019 (Volume 393, Pages 1101–1118). The DOI for this publication is 10.1016/S0140-6736(18)32427-9. 2. Boerman T, Requejo J, Victora CG, Amouzou A, George A, Agyepong I, and colleagues authored a paper titled Countdown to 2030: Tracking Progress Towards Universal Coverage for Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, and Child Health, published in The Lancet in 2018 (Volume 391, Pages 1538–1548). The DOI for this publication is 10.1016/S0140-6736(18)30104-1. 3. UNICEF has developed the Measuring Mental Health Among Adolescents at the Population Level (MMAP) initiative, which focuses on assessing mental health in adolescents. This resource is accessible at unicef.org under the child health and mental health sections, last accessed on May 6, 2023. 4. Guthold R, Moller A-B, Azzopardi P, Ba MG, Fagan L, Baltag V, and colleagues introduced the Global Action for Measurement of Adolescent Health (GAMA) initiative, which aims to redefine adolescent health metrics. This work was published in Journal of Adolescent Health in 2019 (Volume 64, Pages 697–699). The DOI is 10.1016/j.jadohealth.2019.00862. 5. The GAMA initiative also maintains a webpage providing further details about its objectives and activities. This resource is available at int/groups/the-global-action-for-measurement-of-adolescent-health and was last accessed on May 6, 2023. 6. The DHS Program offers high-quality information to plan, monitor, and improve population, health, and nutrition programs. This resource is accessible at dhsprogram.com and was last accessed on February 1, 2023. 7. UNICEF’s Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys (MICS) provide critical data for monitoring child and maternal health. These surveys are available at mics.unicef.org/surveys and were last accessed on February 1, 2023. 8. The World Health Organization (WHO) provides resources on noncommunicable disease surveillance, monitoring, and reporting. These materials are accessible at int/teams/noncommunicable-diseases/surveillance and were last accessed on May 6, 2023. 9. The Health Behaviour in School-aged Children (HBSC) study focuses on understanding health behaviors among school-aged children. This resource is available at hbsc.org and was last accessed on February 1, 2023. 10. Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (CRVS) systems are essential for collecting data on births, deaths, and other vital events. Information on CRVS is available at int/data/data-collection-tools/civil-registration-and-vital-statistics-(crvs) and was last accessed on February 1, 2023. 11. WHO provides a webpage on integrating rehabilitation into health systems, which includes relevant information and resources. This page is accessible at int/activities/integrating-rehabilitation-into-health-systems/information and was last accessed on February 1, 2023. 12. The WHO Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health and Ageing Data Portal offers static visualizations and data on these health areas. This portal is accessible at platform.int/data/maternal-newborn-child-adolescent-ageing/static-visualizations and was last accessed on June 26, 2023. 13. The Adolescent Data Portal provides access to global data on adolescent health. This resource is available at adolescentdata.org/adp and was last accessed on September 27, 2022. 14. The Adolescents and Youth Dashboard offers a comprehensive overview of data related to adolescent and youth health. This dashboard is accessible at adolescentdata.org/data/dashboard/adolescent-youth and was last accessed on February 1, 2023. 15. Guthold R, Baltag V, Katwan E, Lopez G, Diaz T, and Ross DA highlighted the importance of easy access to global, regional, and national adolescent health data through the WHO Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health and Ageing Data Portal. This work was published in Journal of Adolescent Health in 2021 (Volume 68, Pages 243–245). 16. The WHO NCD Microdata Repository provides access to noncommunicable disease-related data. This resource is available at extranet.int and was last accessed in 2023. 17. WHO’s Inequality Monitoring in Sexual, Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health publication provides guidelines for addressing health disparities. This document is accessible at int/publications/item/9789240042438 and was last accessed on September 23, 2022. 18. Diaz T, Strong KL, Cao B, Guthold R, Moran AC, Moller A-B, and colleagues called for standardized age-disaggregated health data in their publication in The Lancet in 2021 (Volume 2, Pages e436–e443). The DOI is 10.1016/S2666-7568(21)00115-X. 19. WHO’s Primary Health Care Measurement Framework and Indicators provide tools for monitoring health systems through a primary health care lens. This resource is accessible at int/publications/item/9789240044210 and was last accessed on May 6, 2023. 20. WHO’s guiding principles for health program evaluation emphasize its application in national health development. This document is accessible at int/publications/item/global-standards-for-health-promoting-schools and was last accessed on May 6, 2023. 21. WHO’s platform for monitoring, evaluation, and review of national health strategies provides a country-led approach to information and accountability. This resource is accessible at int/iris/handle/10665/85877 and was last accessed on May 6, 2023. 22. The OECD’s principles for evaluating development assistance are available in a PDF document, which was last accessed on May 6, 2023. 23. Sebire SJ, Banfield K, Jago R, Edwards MJ, Campbell R, Kipping R, and colleagues conducted a process evaluation of the PLAN-A intervention, a peer-led physical activity program for adolescent girls. This study was published in BMC Public Health in 2019 (Volume 19, Pages 1–13). The DOI is 10.1186/s12889-019-7545-z. 24. WHO’s webpage on working together for health and sustainable development provides resources and information. This page is accessible at int and was last accessed on May 13, 2023. 25. Henrich J, Heine SJ, and Norenzayan A authored a paper titled The Weirdest People in the World? published in Behavioral and Brain Sciences in 2010 (Volume 33, Pages 61–83, with discussion on Pages 135). The DOI is 10.1017/S0140525X0999152X. 26. Lansford JE and Banati P edited the Handbook of Adolescent Development Research and Its Impact on Global Policy. 27. Banati P and Bacalso C conducted a multi-country study on risk and protective factors for emotional and behavioral problems among early adolescents. This study was published in Journal of Youth Development in 2021 (Volume 16, Pages 124–158). 28. The Global Financing Facility (GFF) strategy and country results were reviewed in a stocktaking document, accessible at gff.org/sites/gff_new/files/documents/GFF-IG15-2-Stocktaking.pdf, last accessed on June 19, 2023. 29. Armstrong A, Nagata JM, Vicari M, Irvine C, Cluver L, Sohn AH, and colleagues developed a global research agenda for adolescents living with HIV. This work was published in Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2018 (Volume 78, Supplement 1, Pages S16–S21). 30. The COVID-19 Research Prioritization Group on Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health identified global research priorities on COVID-19 for these populations. This work was published in Journal of Global Health in 2021 (Volume 11, Article 04071). 31. Hindin MJ, Christiansen CS, and Ferguson BJ set research priorities for adolescent sexual and reproductive health in lowand middle-income countries. This work was published in Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2013 (Volume 91, Pages 10–18). 32. Nagata JM, Ferguson BJ, and Ross DA identified research priorities for eight areas of adolescent health in lowand middle-income countries. This work was published in Journal of Adolescent Health in 2016 (Volume 59, Pages 50–60). 33. Svanemyr J, Chandra-Mouli V, Raj A, Travers E, and Sundaram L outlined research priorities for ending child marriage and supporting married girls. This work was published in Reproductive Health in 2015 (Volume 12, Article 80). 34. Rudan I, Gibson JL, Ameratunga S, El Arifeen S, Bhutta ZA, Black M, and colleagues developed guidelines for implementing the CHNRI method to set priorities in global child health research investments. This work was published in Croatian Medical Journal in 2008 (Volume 49, Pages 720–733). 35. Santelli J, Haerizadeh S, and McGovern T emphasized the importance of obtaining informed consent when conducting research with adolescents. This resource is accessible in HTML format and was last accessed on September 27, 2022. 36. Guthold R, Kann L, Bhatti L, Abduvahobov P, Ansong J, Atkinson, and colleagues evaluated the effectiveness of a participatory approach to developing school health interventions in four low-resource cities. This study protocol, titled Empowering Adolescents to Lead Change Using Health Data, is part of a cluster randomized controlled trial and is in press in BMJ Open.
